Command: A brother shall marry his dead brother's widow
Summary: One of the family laws of Deuteronomy 21–25: a brother shall marry his dead brother's widow. These laws protected the weaker party at each family step.
Commandment: A brother shall marry his dead brother's widow
Application: These civil provisions belonged to ancient Israel's family law and have passed with it; the protection of the weaker party they aimed at remains the lesson.
Purpose: To preserve the dead brother's name and inheritance in Israel: the child of the union carries the dead man's name (Deuteronomy 25:5-6).
Function: This one speaks to character, not to courts, though its form belonged to Israel's day. One of the family laws of Deuteronomy 21–25: a brother shall marry his dead brother's widow. Its goal was to preserve the dead brother's name and inheritance in Israel: the child of the union carries the dead man's name. A practical fence, not a decoration. These civil provisions belonged to ancient Israel's family law and have passed with it.
